text:
maya: Heads up — ~12 GPU nodes in us-west2 are NotReady and have the node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoSchedule taint. A bunch of gpu pods are Pending. Autoscaler isn't bringing healthy replacements. Anyone seeing this? :eyes:

samir: seeing it too. New spot nodes are coming up but nvidia-device-plugin is crashlooping on them. Logs show missing nvml / driver build failures.

lina: quick note — these are spot instances booting COS image with kernel 535 but our driver DS is pinned to 530. Kernel module fails to compile -> device plugin can't register.

samir: device-plugin log snippet:
```
I0412 09:42:17.123456 1 nvidia.go:212] Starting NVIDIA device plugin
E0412 09:42:18.234567 1 nvidia.go:295] failed to load libnvidia-ml: libnvidia-ml.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
E0412 09:42:18.234890 1 plugin.go:210] rpc error: code = Unknown desc = device plugin registration failed: failed to find /dev/nvidiactl
```

derek: autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up attempts but then "scale up skipped: insufficient resources" and some errors about taints. I think CA sees NotReady nodes and can't allocate GPUs properly.

ops-bot: Deploy bot triggered rolling update for node pool gpu-spot-usw2 to use driver-version=535-image. Link: https://infra/redeploy/1234

maya: workaround plan: cordon + drain a handful of affected spot nodes (to avoid mass preemption) and restart the nvidia driver DS after patching it to a compatible driver image. Commands I'll run if approved:
```
kubectl cordon <node-name>
kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl -n kube-system set image ds/nvidia-driver nvidia-driver=registry/repo/nvidia-driver:535
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/nvidia-driver
```

lina: agreed. Also long-term: we should bake GPU drivers into the node image or use GKE GPU node image to avoid kernel mismatch on spot boots. Preemptions + driver rebuild is killing stability. I'll open INFRA-432 to track image baking and a policy for pinned kernels.

samir: Oncall @derek or @maya — I'll push the DS image update and restart now. Will cordon/drain 3 nodes first.

derek: go for it. note: set cluster-autoscaler expander to least-waste or add fallback nodegroup so CA can make progress while spots churn. Right now CA is confused because tainted/notready nodes look like capacity but are unusable.

samir: restarted DS at 09:56. Watching logs. Initial checks show device plugin registering on 8 nodes so far.

ops-bot: system: after DS restart, 8 / 12 problematic nodes became Ready and GPU pods started scheduling. 4 nodes were preempted by cloud provider.

maya: nice — that matches what I'm seeing. Still want INFRA ticket for baking drivers + change spot config. Cost note: spot churn added extra provisioning cost and throttled our batch jobs yesterday.

lina: filed INFRA-432: "GPU node image & driver management for spot stability" with proposed owners and rollout plan.

derek: leaving this thread open until autoscaler stops reporting errors and spot churn subsides. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: closing condition met? cluster-autoscaler error rate dropped to baseline and pending GPU pods are down to 1. Marking for follow-up in INFRA-432.
